data.title: Hue Light Control
data.name: Hue Light Control
data.subtitle: A physical control for everyday lighting.
data.summary:
Hue Light Control brings everyday room lighting back to a physical control. Turn the rotary encoder to dim a Philips Hue room or zone, tap to switch it on or off, and hold to open settings on a 128×64 OLED. The finished controller combines an ESP32, a push-button encoder, and an SSD1306 display.

Input and display updates stay responsive while a separate network task sends HTTPS commands to the Hue bridge over the local network. The firmware reuses its connection, batches brightness changes, and reconciles the display with the bridge. On-device diagnostics explain Wi-Fi, authorization, room, display, and memory problems; reconnects, bridge rediscovery, saved settings, and a watchdog help it recover. Bridge discovery uses mDNS first, with Philips’ internet discovery service as an optional fallback.

This is a completed hardware and firmware project, built for one room or zone and documented with pin assignments, setup instructions, and recovery procedures. The portfolio media is technical illustration of the documented components, rather than photography of the assembled device.
data.oneLiner: A physical Philips Hue controller built with an ESP32, rotary encoder, and OLED display.
